To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CCR6 is up‐regulated on tissue‐derived T‐cells and CCL20 is induced during the asthmatics late response.

CCR6 is preferentially expressed by CD4+ T lymphocyte subpopulations in tissues compared with the blood, that CCR6‐mediated chemotaxis of peripheral blood T lymphocytes is enhanced by prior activation, that CCR7 is expressed on the majority of peripheral blood and tissue‐derived memory T cells and that CCL20 is up‐regulated in bronchoalveloal lavage fluid following allergen provocation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of C‐C chemokines in human allergic disease and in particular the C‐C chemokin receptor, CCR6 and its ligand, CCL20.
the mechanisms of T cell recruitment and retention in tissue, and the potential for therapeutic manipulation of these processes.
the role of chemokines in allergic disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

1) CCR6 is expressed on peripheral blood and tissue CD4+ T lymphocyte subpopulations; 2) CCR6 expression is increased on tissue CD4+ lymphocytes compared with peripheral blood CD4+ lymphocyte subpopulators and 3) CCL20 is increased in the bronchoalveolair lavage of asthmatics after endobronchical allergen provocation.
the CCR6+CD4+ T cell population is elevated in tissues compared with the blood in healthy subjects and that CCR6 is up‐regulated in asthmatic airways after allergen provocation.
CCR6 is a key molecule in the regulation of tissue‐specific T‐cell migration and may contribute to the pathogenesis of asthma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of CCR6 is increased on tissue‐derived T lymphocytes, and this may play an important role in the recruitment and retention of effector cells in allergic disease.
CCR6 is important in T cell migration into tissue in health and disease, and that CCL20 may be an important chemoattractant in asthma.
CCR6 is a key player in allergic diseases and its role is not limited to T cells but also includes other cell types.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CCR6 is a marker of tissue‐resident T cells.
the CCR6/CCL20 axis is important in the recruitment of T cells to tissue in allergic disease.
the CCR6/CCL20 axis is a key regulator of T cell migration into the tissues.
